prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / style-transfer.
Input image 1 is the current ROCKY BOARD. This is the PRIMARY reference for the exact ground palette, simple shapes, softness, stone pattern scale and lighting. Input image 2 is the old cave backdrop being REPLACED; discard its side-on composition and dark cave walls completely.
Make the game background feel like an uninterrupted extension of the ground inside image 1. Output a 1536 x 2048 portrait full-bleed environment texture. View the ground DIRECTLY FROM ABOVE, orthographic 90-degree bird's-eye view, like a flat battle map. EVERY part of the canvas, from top to bottom and edge to edge, is WALKABLE FLAT ROCKY GROUND on the same plane. The camera looks straight down at the surface, never forward into a cave. There is no horizon, back wall, ceiling, mountain skyline, doorway, tunnel, cavern opening, distant scenery, perspective convergence, vertical cliff or empty void.
Match the LIGHT warm gray / dusty taupe / very faint lavender colors of the stone INSIDE the reference board, not its dark border. Same brightness and same low contrast as the board floor. A flat matte dusty stone base, broad simple irregular muted gray-lavender patches with soft clean cartoon shapes, and a few tiny low-profile pale angular chips. Sparse stone marks, mostly quiet empty floor. Smooth simple 2-tone cel shading matching the game's item art; no photorealistic texture or grain. All shapes are flush with the ground. Tiny chips stay understated and scattered without any central focal point. Use an even density and even scale over the whole canvas: no larger foreground objects, no darkened corners, no spotlight or gradient toward the center. Small marks remain small after cover cropping, so do not enlarge the reference's pebbles. The center and edges must have the same floor tone so an overlaid matching board reads as a marked area on this very same ground, not a separate pale floating panel.
DO NOT include the board itself, ANY rectangular inset, grid, tile seams, purple divider, outer frame, borders, shadows around a board-shaped area, outlines around ground patches, large rocks, boulders, raised platforms, steps, pits, vegetation, crystals, props, characters, footprints, text or UI. Do not preserve any cave geometry from image 2. This is a single continuous flat rocky surface filling 100% of the image, visually expanding the board floor in every direction. No baked blur. Output the standalone finished background only.
refinement_prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Image 1 is the new overhead rocky ground background to refine. Image 2 is the existing board, supplied ONLY as a stone surface palette/style reference. The output is a 1536 x 2048 full-bleed portrait overhead ground background, no grid and no board.
The ground pattern in image 1 is too large when shown behind the board. ZOOM OUT the texture pattern by a factor of 2.5: every individual color patch and small pebble should be ONLY 40 percent of its current width and height, with about 6 times as many small low-contrast patches across the canvas, irregularly distributed. Do NOT simply scale the whole picture down inside a border. Extend the same continuous stony ground to fill the full canvas edge to edge with the smaller pattern. A few small, pale angular chips distributed lightly, no large visible objects. The texture should be quiet and soft and never a busy speckled noise. Keep broad flat low-contrast cartoon shapes and clean cel shading. Main patches approximately 35–70 output pixels across, tiny chips approximately 7–13 output pixels across. The color patches are subtle tone differences, not dark outlined cracks.
Preserve the light taupe / neutral warm gray / faint lavender FLOOR colors of image 2 with the same brightness, and avoid making the ground more tan, orange or yellow than the reference board. Keep lighting completely flat and even across the canvas. The goal is a field of ground whose small marks visually match the ground inside the overlaid smaller board, so it reads as one continuous surface. No horizon, walls, cave view, platform, frame, grid, tile seams, lines, purple divider, text, rocks larger than tiny chips, creatures, UI or central focal point. Only flat walkable top-down stone ground.
